items.title: 12 Household Bills to Check This Weekend (UK)
items.description: A free UK bill-check checklist: energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, subscriptions, council tax and more. Find £50 a month.

items.title: Paid Every 4 Weeks? You Get 13 Paydays a Year
items.description: If you're paid 4-weekly, you get 13 pay packets a year, not 12. Here's how to budget for it so the extra one isn't wasted.

items.title: Council Tax Over 10 Months? Budget It Over 12
items.description: Council tax is often paid in 10 instalments. Spread the cost over 12 months in your budget so Feb and March feel like bonus months.

items.title: Sinking Funds Every UK Family Needs
items.description: Six sinking funds that stop big yearly costs landing on a credit card: Christmas, MOT, birthdays, holidays, school and TV licence.

items.title: Debt Snowball vs Avalanche: Which Is Better?
items.description: Snowball clears small debts first for quick wins. Avalanche clears high-interest debt first and usually costs less. Compare both.

items.title: Save for Christmas in 12 Months: £50 a Month
items.description: Put £50 a month aside from January and you'll have £600 for Christmas. A sinking fund tracker shows exactly how much to save.

items.title: How to Make a Monthly Budget in 5 Steps
items.description: A simple monthly budget method for UK households: income, bills, everyday spending, savings, and a weekly 2-minute check.

items.title: Find Forgotten Subscriptions in Your Bank App
items.description: Search your banking app for repeating payments and cancel anything you haven't used this month. Part of a free UK bill checklist.

items.title: Do You Need a TV Licence? Quick UK Guide
items.description: You need a TV licence to watch live TV or use BBC iPlayer. If you only stream on-demand from other services, you may not.

items.title: Live Alone? Claim 25% Off Council Tax
items.description: If you're the only adult in your home you can usually get a 25% single person discount on council tax. Apply via your council.

items.title: How to Make a Debt Payoff Plan
items.description: List balances, interest rates and minimum payments, pick one monthly amount and see your debt-free date. Snowball and avalanche compared.

items.title: Zero-Based Budgeting: Give Every Pound a Job
items.description: Zero-based budgeting means income minus everything you plan equals zero. Leftover money goes to a savings pot or debt.

items.title: 5 Easy Ways to Cut Your Food Shop (UK)
items.description: Plan five dinners, shop with a list, switch to own-brand and use what's in the freezer. Small habits that cut the weekly shop.

items.title: How Big Should an Emergency Fund Be?
items.description: Start with one month of essential bills, then build to three. A savings goals tracker works out the monthly amount.

items.title: Yearly Car Costs to Budget For (UK)
items.description: MOT, service, insurance, road tax, tyres and breakdown cover. Turn each into a monthly sinking fund so they're never a surprise.

items.title: The 2-Minute Weekly Budget Habit
items.description: Spend two minutes every Sunday logging the week's spending. A good budget spreadsheet does the rest.

items.title: Broadband Out of Contract? How to Pay Less
items.description: Broadband prices often rise after your contract ends. Get a quote, ask your provider to match it, or ask about social tariffs.

items.title: Which Debt Method Saves Most Interest?
items.description: The avalanche method usually saves the most interest. The snowball method gives quicker wins. Compare both on your own debts.

items.title: UK Household Budget Categories Checklist
items.description: Every category a UK household budget needs, from council tax and TV licence to groceries, fuel and savings pots.

items.title: Why Named Savings Pots Work Better
items.description: Give every savings pot a name and a date. Named goals are easier to stick to than one general savings account.

items.title: How to Pay Less for Your Mobile Phone (UK)
items.description: Move to SIM-only once your handset is paid off, check your data use and set a reminder for when your contract ends.

items.title: Why Left Over £0 Is a Good Budget
items.description: In a zero-based budget, £0 left to assign means every pound is planned: bills, spending, savings and debt.

items.title: Which Debts to Pay First (UK)
items.description: Priority bills like rent, council tax and energy come before credit cards and loans. Free debt help is available from StepChange.

items.title: Car & Home Insurance: Never Auto-Renew
items.description: Get quotes three to four weeks before your car or home insurance renews. It's one of the easiest checks on our free list.

items.title: Yearly Bills That Catch UK Families Out
items.description: Annual costs like the TV licence, MOT, boiler service and Christmas. Save a little each month in a sinking fund.

items.title: Budget Spreadsheets in Light and Dark Mode
items.description: Every Home Sorted planner comes in light and dark editions for Excel and Google Sheets.

items.title: Home Money Kit: Budget, Debt & Savings Spreadsheets
items.description: Three UK household planners in one bundle: budget and bills, debt payoff and sinking funds. Excel and Google Sheets.

items.title: Start Your Budget Before January
items.description: Set up your budget in December so January starts with a plan. Works with any start month, including the April tax year.

items.title: Quick Energy Bill Checks for UK Homes
items.description: Give meter readings, check whether your fixed deal has ended, compare tariffs and make sure your direct debit matches your use.

items.title: New to Budgeting? Start Here (UK)
items.description: Start with the free bill checklist to find savings, then use a UK budget planner to give every pound a job.
